question: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?

In my last internship I was responsible for migrating 800 customer records into our new CRM. I created a checklist of required fields and ran a script to flag missing values before import. After the first batch I caught three duplicates that would have broken reporting, so I added a manual spot-check on 10% of records and asked my mentor to review the edge cases.
What happened when you found those duplicates?
I paused the migration, documented the pattern, and fixed the source data. My mentor later told me the team used the same checklist on the next project.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?
Internship CRM migration, 800 records
Built checklist + script flags + 10% manual audit
Caught duplicates, paused, fixed source
Follow-up: Mentor adopted checklist for next project
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. The candidate owned a concrete data task and built a repeatable process after an early error. Quote: "I paused the migration, documented the pattern, and fixed the source data." The story shows they sought feedback and left a usable artifact rather than just finishing their piece. Biggest strength is turning a mistake into a team-level improvement at an individual-contributor scope.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?

I led the quarterly financial reconciliation between our billing system and the general ledger across three teams. I built a shared validation matrix and required each team to sign off on deltas before close. One month we found a $42k misallocation that would have hit revenue recognition; we traced it to a config change in the payment processor.
How did you get the other teams to adopt the matrix?
I ran a 30-minute walkthrough showing the prior quarter's errors and let them suggest fields. Two teams added their own checks after that.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?

When I took over the compliance reporting team we had three late filings in the prior year due to missed data points. I introduced a RACI matrix plus staged peer reviews with explicit checklists. After six months we had zero late filings and audit findings dropped from 11 to 2.
How did you handle the person who kept missing items?
I paired them with a strong reviewer for two cycles and gave them the checklist as a template. Their error rate fell and they later became the reviewer for new hires.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a job or project where great attention to detail was critical. How did you ensure accuracy?

Before a major acquisition close we discovered inconsistencies in the target company's customer contract data across four legacy systems. I stood up a cross-functional data integrity task force with weekly exec reviews and required sign-off from legal, finance, and ops before signing. The diligence uncovered $18M in unrecognized liabilities that changed the final price.
How did you decide what level of detail was enough?
We set materiality thresholds by contract size and risk category, then sampled below the threshold. The board accepted the approach because we documented the residual risk.
